explanations: redeem() reads the redemption count with get(), compares it to the limit, and writes back count + 1 with set(). Those are three separate round trips, so during a rush many checkouts read the same value, all pass the check, and all write the same count + 1. Redemptions are granted far past the limit, and the counter itself loses increments. The store already offers an atomic incrBy. The fix claims a redemption with incrBy(key, 1) and checks the value it returns, which is unique to each caller. If that value is over the limit, it gives the claim back with incrBy(key, -1) and rejects with sold_out. The check and the increment become one atomic step, and release()'s atomic decrement can no longer be overwritten by a stale set().
